To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Lindenmayer systems can be used to model biological and robotic systems; (2) Lindenmayer representations of such systems can be placed under feedback control; and (3) the incorporation of feedback in such models has implications for biological and robotic design.
The incorporation of feedback control in generative Lindenmayer systems provides a powerful framework for modeling biological and robotic systems, including the evolution of such systems."

the incorporation of feedback control into the evolution of generative context-sensitive Lindenmayer systems can be accomplished by modifying the rules of a generative context-sensitive L-system in a manner similar to the way in which the rules of a non-context-sensitive L-system can be modified to place it under feedback control, except for the addition of a new rule that is used to reset the feedback control mechanism.

modeling biological and robotic systems with generative L systems.
the incorporation of feedback into the modeling of biological systems.
modeling biological systems, and with the development of robots and other machines that can be used in the study of biological systems.

the evolution of generative Lindenmayer systems is an area which is still in need of research.

feedback and feedback control are important and essential for biological modeling and robot design.

we are proposing a new class of L-systems, the parametric Lindenmeyer systems under context sensitive feedback control.

the use of Lindenmayer representations in modeling biological and robotic systems has been extended from context-free and context-sensitive L systems to context-sensitive parametric ones, and that the use of feedback control in the evolution of these systems has also been extended to include context-sensitive parametric systems.
